title: Deliver remotely, write clearly, and get paid safely

say: Deliver remotely, write clearly, and get paid safely.
This is the video for module 2: Remote Delivery Standards, Tools, Communication and Getting Paid Safely.
In an office, a manager can walk to your desk. In remote work, your tools are your desk: one tidy shared folder, a task board, a call that starts on time.

say: When you share in Google Drive, you choose a role. A Viewer can only open and read.

panel.heading: Give the smallest role they need

cards.d: Open and read only. For final reports, invoices and portfolio samples.
Can suggest and comment, but not change the text. Best for client drafts.
Can change, delete and share further. Only for team members working in the file.

say: A Commenter can suggest changes but not alter your text. Give clients this for drafts, so the original stays safe. Share to their named email, not anyone with the link, because a link can be forwarded.

say: An Editor can change and delete, so keep that for people who must work in the file.
And if a client says you deleted their paragraph, open File, then Version history. It shows who changed what, calmly.

say: Tell the client as soon as you see a risk, not on the deadline day.

panel.heading: Warning about a delay
items: Warn as soon as you see the risk
Say what happened in one sentence
Offer the client two choices
Confirm call or WhatsApp agreements by email

say: Explain in one sentence, without long excuses. For example, a power outage has slowed the video edit.

panel.heading: Warning about a delay

Offer the client two choices
Confirm call or WhatsApp agreements by email

say: Then offer choices: the full video on Thursday, or the first 60 seconds on Wednesday as planned and the rest on Thursday. Which do you prefer?

say: And when something is agreed on a call, follow up with a short email: as agreed on our call today. That becomes your record.

say: A real client pays you for agreed work, uses an official email or platform, and is happy to sign a simple agreement.

panel.heading: Real client or scam?
right: Asks you to pay a fee first

say: A scammer asks you to pay first, or sends too much and asks for a refund before the money has cleared. Refund only after your bank confirms it, and only to the original source.
Never trust a screenshot. Only trust your own bank or app balance.

panel.heading: Real client or scam?
right: Asks you to pay a fee first

say: Use a different strong password for your email, bank and work platforms. Turn on 2-Step Verification, and set a WhatsApp two-step PIN.
Never share a one-time code, even with someone who says they are from your bank. And with new clients, ask for part of the fee before you start, for example 50%.

panel.heading: Your account safety checklist
items: A different strong password for each account
2-Step Verification on Google and platforms
A WhatsApp two-step PIN
Never share a one-time code (OTP)
New clients: a deposit, for example 50%

say: To remember. Share with the smallest role. Send regular updates so no one chases you. Warn about delays early. Know your net amount before you agree a price. And never pay to get work, or share a code.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Smallest Drive role; version history as proof
Updates: Done, Next, Blockers
Warn about delays early, with options
Calculate your net amount before pricing
Never pay to work, never share an OTP
